title: Evaluation of Cardiac Contractility Modulation Therapy in 2D Human Stem Cell-Derived Cardiomyocytes
protocol: Prepare a sterile 6-well plate by transferring 2 mL of 0.1% gelatin to each well.
Incubate the coated plate at 37°C for a minimum of 1 hour.
Thaw a hydrogel aliquot in the refrigerator on ice one day before seeding hiPSC-CMs.
Mix 500 mL of RPMI 1640, 10 mL of 50x B-27 Supplement, and 5 mL of penicillin-streptomycin to prepare cardiomyocyte medium.
Pre-plate the hiPSC-CMs on 0.1% gelatin-coated sterile 6-well plates two days before seeding them on the hydrogel substrate.
Thaw the hiPSC-CMs using a standard thawing protocol.
Plate 1,500,000 total hiPSC-CMs per well according to manufacturer's instructions.
Culture the hiPSC-CMs in cardiomyocyte medium for 2-4 days at 37°C and 5% CO2.
Refresh spent medium with 100% cardiomyocyte medium every 48 hours.
Check the status of the hiPSC-CMs before dissociation to ensure viability and stable beating.
Wash the hiPSC-CMs twice with 4 mL per well of D-PBS without CaCl2 or MgCl2.
Aspirate the D-PBS from each well.
Add 1 mL of room temperature dissociation reagent to each well and incubate for 15 min at 37°C.
Add 10 mL of cardiomyocyte medium to a sterile 15 mL conical tube.
Dissociate the hiPSC-CMs from the 6-well plate with a 1,000 µL pipette.
Transfer the cell suspension to the 15 mL conical tube.
Rinse each well with 1 mL of fresh cardiomyocyte medium and add this to the 15 mL conical tube.
Bring the final volume in the conical tube to 15 mL by adding more medium if necessary.
Centrifuge for 5 min at 200 × g.
Remove the supernatant up to the 1 mL mark.
Resuspend the cells in cardiomyocyte medium to a final volume of 5 mL.
Count the hiPSC-CMs with a manual or automated cell counter.
Incubate the hiPSC-CM suspension at room temperature while preparing the flexible hydrogel substrates (maximum 30 min).
Prepare a 20 µL pipette set at 1 µL and 20 µL pipette tips.
Ensure that a stopwatch/timer is ready ahead of making the hydrogel substrates.
Mix the ECM-based hydrogel substrate by gently tapping the tube.
Place the tube back on ice immediately after mixing.
Start the stopwatch/timer before the first hydrogel substrate is plated.
Pipette 1 µL of the hydrogel substrate up and down ~3x to chill the pipette tip.
Apply ~1 µL of undiluted hydrogel substrate horizontally to the bottom of each well of the 48-well plate.
Hold the pipette at a 45° angle when applying the hydrogel substrate.
Plate all hydrogel substrates in the same orientation in each well.
Prepare hydrogel substrates by pipetting ~1 μL per well in a 48-well plate.
Allow the hydrogel substrates to incubate for 8-10 min at room temperature in a sterile tissue culture hood before adding cells.
Seed hiPSC-CMs dropwise directly onto the hydrogel substrates with approximately 30,000 viable cells per well in ~200 μL of cardiomyocyte medium.
Place the lid on the plate and allow hiPSC-CMs to incubate undisturbed for 10-15 min at room temperature in the sterile tissue culture hood.
Gently add ~100 μL of fresh cardiomyocyte medium to each well (final volume: ~300 μL per well).
Place the lid on the plate and transfer to an incubator at 37 °C, 5% CO2 for 2-4 days.
Refresh the 100% medium every 24 h before contraction experiments are performed.
Visually inspect the hiPSC-CMs for correct morphology immediately after plating; cells should appear round.
By day 2 after seeding, observe a confluent 2D hiPSC-CM monolayer syncytium with robust visible contraction.
Prepare CCM assay medium containing CaCl2 0.5 mmol/L, NaCl 134 mmol/L, KCl 5.4 mmol/L, MgCl2 1 mmol/L, glucose 10 mmol/L, HEPES 10 mmol/L, pH adjusted to 7.4 with NaOH.
Equilibrate the CCM assay medium to 37 °C in a water bath.
Turn on the microscope and environmental control chamber to equilibrate to 37 °C and 5% CO2.
Remove the cardiomyocyte medium from the 48-well plate.
Gently rinse each well twice with 600 μL of CCM assay medium.
Add 300 μL of CCM assay medium per well.
Place the 48-well plate on the microscope in the environmental control chamber.
Insert the electrodes.
Equilibrate the cells for 5 min.
Open the video recording software.
Set a frame rate of 100 frames/s.
Select a region of interest (ROI) near the center of the hiPSC-CM monolayer.
Field stimulate the cells with a commercial pulse generator.
Pace the hiPSC-CMs at 1.5x threshold at 1 Hz with baseline pulse parameters.
Record the baseline, pacing only contraction video for a minimum of five beats.
Stimulate the hiPSC-CM monolayer with an experimental electrical signal using standard CCM stimulation parameters.
Use two symmetrical biphasic pulses of 5.14 ms phase duration and a total duration of 20.56 ms.
Set the phase amplitude to ~28 V/cm.
Ensure zero interphase interval.
Apply a 30 ms delay from the end of the pacing pulse to the beginning of the CCM pulse.
Record the CCM-induced contraction video for a minimum of five beats.
Turn off the CCM signal.
Stimulate with a baseline pacing pulse.
Record a contraction video of the recovery period for a minimum of five beats.
Use standard contraction software to automatically analyze the contraction videos.
Quantify key contractile properties such as the contraction amplitude, contraction slope, relaxation slope, time to peak, time to baseline 90%, and contraction duration 50%.
Conduct contractile experiments with 2D hiPSC-CMs on a flexible hydrogel substrate from days 2-14 after plating.
